reconstructed_theorem: For every complete real inner product space E, every function f:E→ℝ, and every pair of real numbers β,h, assume h≥0, βh≤1, and, for all x,y∈E, f(y)≤f(x)+⟨gradient f(x),y−x⟩+(β/2)‖y−x‖². Here gradient f(x) denotes the Riesz vector of the totalized Fréchet derivative; no separate differentiability hypothesis is imposed, and no positivity hypothesis on β is imposed. For every initial point x₀∈E define xₖ=T^[k](x₀), where T(x)=x−h·gradient f(x), h·v is real scalar multiplication, and x₀ is the zeroth iterate. Then for every natural number N, (h/2)∑_{k=0}^{N−1}‖gradient f(xₖ)‖²≤f(x₀)−f(x_N). The sum runs over exactly the natural numbers k<N. N=0 is included, with empty sum zero and x_N=x₀, so the conclusion is 0≤0. h=0 is also included; all iterates then equal x₀ and both sides vanish. No minimizer or lower bound for f is assumed.

For every complete real inner product space E, every function f:E→ℝ, every pair of real numbers β,h, and every z∈E, assume f(z)≤f(x) for every x∈E, h>0, βh≤1, and, for all x,y∈E, f(y)≤f(x)+⟨gradient f(x),y−x⟩+(β/2)‖y−x‖². Here gradient f(x) denotes the Riesz vector of the totalized Fréchet derivative; no separate differentiability hypothesis is imposed, and no positivity hypothesis on β is imposed. For every initial point x₀∈E, define xₖ=T^[k](x₀), where T(x)=x−h·gradient f(x), h·v is real scalar multiplication, and the zeroth iterate is x₀. For every natural number N>0, there exists a natural number k with 0≤k<N such that ‖gradient f(xₖ)‖≤sqrt(2(f(x₀)−f(z))/((N:ℝ)h)). The square root is the nonnegative real square root, totalized to zero on negative arguments; here its argument is nonnegative because z is a global minimizer and (N:ℝ)h>0. The index set includes k=0 and excludes k=N. N=1 is included and forces k=0. N=0 and h=0 are excluded by the hypotheses. If f(x₀)=f(z), the bound is zero.
